title: Turkey revives F-16 talks with US amid Israel, Greece deterrence concerns
gist: Turkey has resumed talks with the US over buying additional F-16 Block 70s, held at Ramstein Air Base on Sept. 17-18, 2026, as a bridge to cover a looming air-power gap: its F-4E Phantoms near retirement, F-35 access remains uncertain, first Eurofighters are not expected before 2030, and the indigenous KAAN is not yet operational.

insights.claim: Turkey faces a potential combat-aircraft capability gap because its F-4E Phantoms are nearing retirement and its F-16 fleet is ageing, while its next-generation indigenous KAAN fighter is not yet fully operational.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A multi-year gap in Turkish air power shapes its procurement urgency and bargaining position with Washington and European suppliers.
insights.quote: Ankara faces a potential capability gap before its next-generation indigenous fighter, the KAAN, becomes fully operational
insights.locator: With Turkey's aging F-4E Phantoms nearing retirement

insights.claim: Turkey's first Eurofighter Typhoons are not expected to arrive before 2030, so they cannot fill the near-term gap in its fighter fleet.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Delivery timelines push Ankara back toward US platforms for the late-2020s, sustaining demand for Lockheed Martin F-16 production.
insights.quote: its first Eurofighters are not expected before 2030

themes.theme: F-16 Block 70 as bridge and F-35 uncertainty

insights.claim: Lingering uncertainty over whether Turkey can acquire Lockheed Martin F-35s, combined with the need to modernize its ageing fleet, likely drove Ankara's decision to resume talks with Washington on buying more F-16s.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Turkey's return to the F-16 track signals it does not expect an F-35 readmission soon; a deal would be a modest positive for Lockheed Martin and a marker of US-Turkey defense thaw.
insights.quote: Lingering uncertainty over Turkey’s prospects of acquiring Lockheed Martin's F-35 Joint Strike Fighters
insights.locator: ANKARA — Lingering uncertainty over Turkey's prospects

insights.claim: New US-made F-16 Block 70 aircraft could serve as a ready-made bridge for Turkey through the transition to next-generation fighters.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Positions the F-16 Block 70 as an interim solution rather than a long-term platform, limiting the likely size and duration of any order.
insights.quote: The new US-made F-16 Block 70s could provide a ready-made bridge through that transition

insights.claim: Turkish and US air force officials held F-16 talks at Ramstein Air Base in Germany on Sept. 17-18, 2026, according to Turkey's Defense Ministry; the article frames Ankara's motivation around deterrence concerns regarding Israel and Greece.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Formal air-force-level talks indicate the procurement track is active; regional deterrence against Israel and Greece adds a geopolitical dimension that could complicate US congressional approval.
insights.quote: Turkish and US air force officials held talks at Ramstein Air Base in Germany on Sept. 17-18
insights.locator: Turkish and US air force officials held talks
